items.name: Senior Staff Architect Persona
items.summary: Makes your AI review your code like a principal engineer focused on scale and trade-offs.
items.prompt: Act as a Principal Systems Architect. Review the provided code for scale limits, memory leaks, concurrency hazards and idempotency guarantees. Present trade-offs as a Markdown table (option, benefit, cost, when to choose it) and push back on premature optimization.

items.name: Code Explainer for Beginners
items.summary: Explains any code with everyday analogies, common gotchas and a mini quiz.
items.prompt: Explain the following code as if I started programming two weeks ago. Describe each part with an everyday analogy (kitchen, plumbing, mail). Then list the three most common mistakes people make with code like this, and finish with a 3-question self-test with answers hidden at the end. PASTE CODE HERE

items.name: Strict JSON Output
items.summary: Gets back clean JSON that matches a schema you provide, with no extra chatter.

items.name: Write my CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md
items.summary: Has your agent interview you, then write a project instructions file so it understands your project every session.
useCases: set up claude code for my project
make claude remember my project rules
set up codex for my project
items.prompt: Look around this repository, then ask me up to five short questions about anything you could not infer (how to run tests, code style, things to avoid). After I answer, write a concise instructions file (CLAUDE.md for Claude Code, AGENTS.md for Codex and most other agents, GEMINI.md for Gemini CLI) with: how to build/test/run, project layout, conventions, and gotchas. Keep it under 60 lines.

items.name: Reproduce-First Bug Fix
items.summary: Makes your AI reproduce a bug with a failing test before it touches the fix.
items.prompt: Before changing any code: 1) restate the bug in one sentence, 2) write a failing test that reproduces it and show me the failure, 3) explain the root cause. Only then make the smallest fix that turns the test green, and run the full test suite.

items.name: Plain-English PR Description
items.summary: Turns a diff into a pull request description a non-engineer can follow.
useCases: explain my changes to my manager
items.prompt: Write a pull request description for the current diff. Sections: What changed (2-3 bullets in plain English), Why, How to test (numbered steps), Risks. Avoid jargon; if a technical term is needed, define it in parentheses.

items.name: Patient Study Tutor
items.summary: Turns your AI into a tutor that quizzes you and explains what you got wrong.
items.prompt: You are my patient study tutor for [SUBJECT]. First ask me what I already know. Then teach one idea at a time in plain language, with one example each. After every idea, ask me one quiz question and wait for my answer. If I'm wrong, explain why kindly and try a simpler question. Every five questions, summarize what I've mastered and what to review.

items.name: Clear Email Writer
items.summary: Drafts a short, polite email from a few rough notes, in the tone you pick.
items.prompt: Write an email from these rough notes: [NOTES]. Recipient: [WHO]. Tone: [friendly / formal / firm]. Keep it under 150 words, put the main ask in the first two sentences, and end with one clear next step. Give me a subject line and two alternative openings.

items.name: Meeting Notes to Action Items
items.summary: Turns messy meeting notes or a transcript into decisions, owners and deadlines.
items.prompt: Here are notes or a transcript from a meeting: [PASTE]. Give me: 1) a three-sentence summary, 2) decisions made, 3) action items as a table (task, owner, deadline; write 'unassigned' if unclear), 4) open questions. Don't invent anything that isn't in the notes.

items.name: Trip Planner
items.summary: Builds a day-by-day travel itinerary around your budget, pace and interests.
items.prompt: Plan a [NUMBER]-day trip to [PLACE] for [WHO]. Budget: [BUDGET]. We like [INTERESTS] and prefer a [relaxed / packed] pace. Give a day-by-day plan with morning, afternoon and evening, rough costs, travel time between stops, and one rainy-day backup per day. Ask me up to three questions first if anything important is missing.

items.name: Essay Coach
items.summary: Gives honest, specific feedback on your writing without rewriting it for you.
items.prompt: Act as a writing coach. Here is my draft: [PASTE]. Don't rewrite it. Instead: 1) tell me the main argument in one sentence as you understood it, 2) list the three biggest problems (structure, clarity, evidence) with the exact sentence each applies to, 3) point out what works well, 4) suggest one concrete exercise to fix the weakest part.

items.name: Explain Like I'm Five
items.summary: Explains any topic with everyday comparisons, then checks you understood.
items.prompt: Explain [TOPIC] as if I'm completely new to it. Use one everyday comparison, avoid jargon (or define it the first time), and keep it under 200 words. Then ask me one question to check I understood, and offer to go one level deeper.

items.name: Decision Helper
items.summary: Lays out your options, trade-offs and a recommendation for a tough choice.
items.prompt: I need to decide: [DECISION]. Options: [OPTIONS]. What matters most to me: [PRIORITIES]. Ask me clarifying questions if needed, then give a comparison table (option, pros, cons, risks, cost), say which option you'd pick and why, and what would change your mind.

items.name: One-Page Business Plan
items.summary: Turns a business idea into a one-page plan with customers, pricing and first steps.
items.prompt: Help me turn this idea into a one-page business plan: [IDEA]. Cover: the problem, who has it most, the solution, how it makes money and a first price, competitors and why we're different, the riskiest assumption, and three cheap experiments to test it in the next two weeks. Be blunt about weak spots.

items.name: Social Post Writer
items.summary: Writes platform-ready posts for LinkedIn, X or Instagram from one idea.
items.prompt: Turn this into social posts: [IDEA OR LINK SUMMARY]. Write one LinkedIn post (under 150 words, hook in the first line), three X posts (under 280 characters each, different angles) and one Instagram caption with up to five relevant hashtags. Match this voice: [VOICE]. No emojis unless I ask.

items.name: Job Application Helper
items.summary: Tailors your CV and cover letter to a specific job posting.
items.prompt: Here is a job posting: [POSTING]. Here is my CV: [CV]. 1) List the five things this employer cares about most. 2) Show where my CV proves each one, and where it's weak. 3) Write a cover letter under 250 words that leads with my strongest match. 4) Give me five likely interview questions with notes on how I'd answer from my experience.

items.name: Spreadsheet Analyst
items.summary: Finds trends and answers questions about data you paste or upload.
items.prompt: Here is my data (pasted or attached): [DATA]. First describe what each column seems to mean and flag anything odd (blanks, duplicates, outliers). Then answer: [QUESTION]. Show your working as a small table, suggest the one chart that best shows the answer, and list two follow-up questions worth asking.

items.name: Summarize Anything
items.summary: Summarizes an article, video transcript or document at the length you want.
items.prompt: Summarize this: [PASTE TEXT OR TRANSCRIPT]. Give me: a one-sentence TL;DR, five key points as bullets, any numbers or claims worth double-checking, and what the author wants me to do or believe. Keep the whole thing under 200 words.

items.name: Prompt Improver
items.summary: Rewrites a rough request into a clear prompt any AI will follow better.
items.prompt: Improve this prompt so an AI gives a better answer: [MY PROMPT]. Ask me up to three questions about anything missing (goal, audience, format, constraints). Then give the improved prompt, and explain in three bullets what you changed and why.

items.name: Image Prompt Writer
items.summary: Writes detailed prompts for AI image tools (logos, illustrations, photos).
items.prompt: I want an image of: [IDEA]. Use: [logo / illustration / photo / icon]. Write three different prompts for an AI image generator, each with subject, style, composition, lighting, colors and what to avoid. For a logo, keep it simple, flat and readable at small sizes.

items.name: Firebase MCP
items.summary: Lets your AI manage Firebase projects: Firestore data, Auth users, rules, hosting and more.
items.description: Firebase's official MCP server, shipped in the Firebase CLI. Works with Firestore, Authentication, Storage, Remote Config, security rules, Data Connect and Crashlytics.

install.command: claude mcp add firebase -- npx -y firebase-tools@latest mcp
steps: Run the command from your project folder

items.author: Firebase

items.name: MongoDB MCP
items.summary: Lets your AI explore and query your MongoDB or Atlas databases.
items.description: MongoDB's official MCP server: list databases and collections, run find and aggregate queries, inspect schemas and indexes, and manage Atlas clusters.

install.command: claude mcp add mongodb -e MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING=YOUR_CONNECTION_STRING -- npx -y mongodb-mcp-server@latest --readOnly

items.author: MongoDB

items.name: Proofread, Keep My Voice
items.summary: Fixes grammar, spelling and clunky sentences without making your writing sound like an AI.
items.prompt:
Proofread the text below. Fix spelling, grammar, punctuation and sentences that are hard to follow, but keep my wording, tone and length wherever they already work. Don't add new ideas or buzzwords. Return the corrected text, then a short list of the changes that weren't just typos, so I can learn from them.

Text:
[PASTE]

items.name: Rewrite in a Different Tone
items.summary: Rewrites a message shorter, friendlier, firmer or more formal, with three versions to pick from.
items.prompt:
Rewrite the text below to be [shorter / friendlier / more formal / firmer / more confident] for [WHO WILL READ IT]. Keep every fact and request in it. Give me three versions that differ in how far they go, from a light touch to a full rewrite, and say in one line what each one changes.

Text:
[PASTE]

items.name: Natural Translator
items.summary: Translates so it reads like a native speaker wrote it, and flags phrases that don't carry over.
items.prompt:
Translate the text below from [SOURCE LANGUAGE] into [TARGET LANGUAGE] for [AUDIENCE, e.g. a client in Mexico]. Make it sound like a native speaker wrote it, not a word-for-word copy. Keep names, numbers and formatting. After the translation, list any idioms, jokes or cultural references you changed and why, and anything where the right choice depends on context I haven't given you.

Text:
[PASTE]

items.name: Reply to This Email
items.summary: Reads an email you received and drafts a reply that answers every question in it.
items.prompt:
Here is an email I received:
[PASTE EMAIL]

What I want to say back: [YOUR POINTS, OR 'decline politely' / 'say yes but ask for a later date']. Draft a reply that answers every question they asked (list any you can't answer from my notes), matches their level of formality, and stays under 120 words unless more is truly needed.

items.name: Inbox Triage
items.summary: Sorts a pile of pasted emails into reply now, later, delegate or ignore, with draft replies for the urgent ones.
items.prompt:
Below are several emails, separated by ---. For each one, give: sender, a one-line summary, a category (reply today / reply this week / delegate / just read / ignore) and why. Then draft short replies for everything marked 'reply today'. Flag anything that looks like a deadline, a payment, or phishing.

[PASTE EMAILS]

items.name: Say the Hard Thing
items.summary: Helps you word a tough message: saying no, an apology, a complaint, or setting a boundary.
items.prompt: Help me write a message to [WHO] about [SITUATION]. I want to [say no / apologize / complain / ask for something / set a boundary] without being rude or over-apologizing. Our relationship: [e.g. coworker, landlord, friend]. Give me a short version and a warmer version, and point out any sentence that could be read as passive-aggressive.

items.name: Customer Support Reply
items.summary: Writes a calm, helpful reply to a customer message, following your policy.
items.prompt:
You're replying on behalf of [BUSINESS]. Our policy on this: [POLICY, e.g. refunds within 30 days]. Customer message:
[PASTE]

Write a reply that acknowledges the problem in their words, says clearly what we can and can't do and why, gives the next step with a timeframe, and stays friendly even if they're angry. No corporate filler. If their request falls outside the policy, offer the closest thing we can do.

items.name: Product Description Writer
items.summary: Turns product details into a short, honest description for a store listing.
items.prompt: Write a product listing for: [PRODUCT]. Details: [MATERIALS, SIZE, FEATURES, PRICE]. Who buys it: [CUSTOMER]. Give a title under 70 characters, a two-sentence description that leads with the main benefit, five bullet points (benefit first, then the feature that delivers it), and ten search keywords. Don't claim anything that isn't in the details.

items.name: Repurpose One Piece of Content
items.summary: Turns one article, talk or video transcript into a newsletter, posts and a short summary.
items.prompt: Here is something I made: [PASTE ARTICLE OR TRANSCRIPT]. Turn it into: 1) a newsletter section (150 words, one clear takeaway, one link placeholder), 2) three social posts with different hooks, 3) a 50-word summary for my website. Keep my voice and examples; don't invent stats.

items.name: Weekly Status Update
items.summary: Turns rough bullet notes into a clear weekly update for your team or manager.
items.prompt: Turn my notes into a weekly update for [AUDIENCE]. Notes: [PASTE]. Format: Done this week, Next week, Blockers or help needed, and one line on the most important thing. Use plain sentences, put numbers and dates where I gave them, and keep it under 200 words. Ask me if a blocker is missing an owner.

items.name: Meeting Agenda
items.summary: Builds a timed agenda with a goal for each item, so the meeting ends with decisions.
items.prompt: Make an agenda for a [LENGTH]-minute meeting about [TOPIC] with [WHO]. What we need to leave with: [DECISIONS OR OUTCOMES]. Give each item a time box, an owner and whether it's to inform, discuss or decide. Add three questions to send people beforehand, and suggest anything that could be an email instead.

items.name: Presentation Outline
items.summary: Plans a talk or slide deck: the story, one message per slide, and speaker notes.
items.prompt: I'm presenting [TOPIC] to [AUDIENCE] for [MINUTES] minutes. I want them to [DECISION OR ACTION]. Outline the deck: one headline sentence per slide (the point, not the topic), what goes on each slide, and two lines of speaker notes. Keep it to [NUMBER] slides, put the main ask early, and end with the one thing they should remember.

items.name: Turn a Process into a Checklist
items.summary: Writes a step-by-step checklist or SOP from how you describe doing a task.
items.prompt: Here's how I do [TASK], in my own words: [DESCRIBE]. Turn it into a checklist someone new could follow without asking me: numbered steps, what 'done' looks like for each, the tools or logins needed, common mistakes, and what to do if a step fails. Ask me about any step that's vague before you finish.

items.name: Constructive Feedback
items.summary: Helps you write specific, kind feedback for a review, a colleague or a report.
items.prompt: Help me write feedback for [PERSON / ROLE] covering [PERIOD]. What went well: [NOTES]. What should change: [NOTES]. For each point, give the specific behavior, its impact and a concrete suggestion. Keep it honest but kind, avoid vague praise like 'great job', and end with one clear goal for next time.

items.name: Spreadsheet Formula Helper
items.summary: Writes the Excel or Google Sheets formula for what you describe, and explains it.
items.prompt: I'm using [Excel / Google Sheets]. My columns: [e.g. A = date, B = customer, C = amount]. I want: [WHAT YOU WANT, e.g. total per customer for March]. Give me the formula, where to put it, and a plain-English explanation of each part. If there's a simpler way (a pivot table or filter), tell me that too.

items.name: SQL Query Writer
items.summary: Writes a SQL query from a plain-English question and your table layout, and explains it.
items.prompt: My database is [Postgres / MySQL / SQLite / BigQuery]. Tables and columns: [PASTE SCHEMA OR DESCRIBE]. Question: [WHAT YOU WANT TO KNOW]. Write the query, explain each part in a sentence, and point out any assumption you made (e.g. how you handled duplicates or missing values). Prefer read-only queries; warn me before anything that changes data.

items.name: Research Brief
items.summary: Gives a balanced overview of a topic, separates facts from opinions, and says what's uncertain.
items.prompt: Give me a research brief on [TOPIC] for [PURPOSE]. Cover: the key facts, the main points of disagreement and who holds each view, recent developments (say the date your information goes up to), and what's still unknown. Mark anything you're not sure about. If you can browse, cite sources with links; if you can't, say so and suggest what to search for.

items.name: Explain This Document
items.summary: Explains a contract, policy, letter or form in plain English and lists what you need to do.
items.prompt:
Explain the document below in plain English. Tell me: what it is, what I'm agreeing to or being asked to do, deadlines and costs, anything unusual or one-sided, and questions I should ask before signing or replying. This isn't legal or financial advice; tell me if something is serious enough that I should ask a professional.

[PASTE DOCUMENT]

items.name: Flashcards from My Notes
items.summary: Turns notes or a chapter into question-and-answer flashcards you can import into Anki or Quizlet.
items.prompt:
Make flashcards from the material below. One fact or idea per card, questions that test understanding rather than copying a sentence, and short answers. Include a few cards that ask 'why' or 'what's the difference between'. Output as two columns separated by a tab (question, answer) so I can import them into Anki or Quizlet.

[PASTE NOTES]

items.name: Language Practice Partner
items.summary: Chats with you in the language you're learning and gently corrects your mistakes.
items.prompt: Be my conversation partner in [LANGUAGE]. My level: [beginner / intermediate / advanced]. Topic: [e.g. ordering food, a job interview]. Write short replies at my level and ask me questions to keep the conversation going. After each of my messages, show my mistakes corrected in brackets with a one-line explanation in English, then continue the conversation.

items.name: Step-by-Step How-To
items.summary: Explains how to do any practical task in numbered steps, with what you'll need and what can go wrong.
items.prompt: Walk me through how to [TASK]. My situation: [e.g. tools I have, device, experience level]. Start with what I need before I begin, then numbered steps with one action each, how to tell each step worked, and the common mistakes. Stop after [5] steps and ask if I'm ready for the rest if it's long. Tell me when this is a job for a professional.

items.name: Weekly Meal Plan and Grocery List
items.summary: Plans a week of meals around your diet, budget and time, with one combined shopping list.
useCases: what should i cook this week
items.prompt: Plan [NUMBER] dinners [and lunches] for this week for [WHO, e.g. 2 adults, 1 child]. Diet or allergies: [DETAILS]. Budget: [AMOUNT]. Time on weeknights: [MINUTES]. Reuse ingredients across meals to cut waste, include one batch-cook day, and end with a grocery list grouped by store aisle with quantities. Note which items I probably already have.

items.name: Cook with What I Have
items.summary: Suggests recipes from the ingredients already in your fridge and cupboard.
items.prompt: I have: [INGREDIENTS]. Equipment: [e.g. oven, air fryer]. Time: [MINUTES]. Suggest three dishes I can make mostly from these, saying which extra ingredients each needs. Then give the full recipe for the one with the fewest extras, with steps and timings.

items.name: Plan My Week
items.summary: Turns a messy to-do list into a realistic weekly schedule, with priorities and breaks.
items.prompt: Here's everything on my plate: [BRAIN DUMP]. Fixed commitments: [MEETINGS, CLASSES, PICKUPS]. I'm most focused [mornings / afternoons / evenings]. Sort the tasks into must / should / could, estimate how long each takes, and lay them out across [DAYS] without filling every hour. Tell me what to drop or delay if it doesn't fit.

items.name: Beginner Workout Plan
items.summary: Builds a simple weekly workout plan around your goal, equipment and time.
items.prompt: Make a [NUMBER]-week workout plan. Goal: [e.g. get stronger, run 5k]. Days per week: [NUMBER], [MINUTES] each. Equipment: [e.g. none, dumbbells, gym]. Limitations: [INJURIES OR NONE]. Give each session with exercises, sets, reps or time, and an easier option for each. Explain how to progress each week. Remind me to check with a doctor if I have health conditions.

items.name: Compare Before I Buy
items.summary: Compares products or services on what matters to you and recommends one.
items.prompt: I'm choosing between [OPTIONS] (or help me find options for [NEED]). Budget: [AMOUNT]. What matters most: [PRIORITIES]. Compare them in a table on those points, plus price, known problems and running costs. Recommend one for my situation and say what would make another option the better pick. Say when your information may be out of date.

items.name: Sort My Spending
items.summary: Groups a list of expenses into categories and shows where the money goes. Not financial advice.
items.prompt: Here are my expenses for [MONTH] (date, description, amount): [PASTE]. Group them into categories, total each one, and show the share of my spending. Point out subscriptions, repeat charges and anything that looks unusual. Then suggest three places to cut that wouldn't change my life much. This is for organizing, not financial advice.

items.name: Gift and Idea Generator
items.summary: Brainstorms gift, name or activity ideas that fit the person, budget and occasion.
items.prompt: Brainstorm [gift / party / name / date] ideas for [WHO OR WHAT]. About them: [INTERESTS, AGE, PERSONALITY]. Budget: [AMOUNT]. Occasion: [OCCASION]. Give 15 ideas in three groups (safe, thoughtful, surprising), one line each on why it fits. Avoid generic picks like gift cards unless I ask.

items.name: Commit Message from a Diff
items.summary: Writes a clear commit message from your staged changes.
items.prompt:
Write a commit message for this diff. Subject line under 72 characters in the imperative mood ("Add", "Fix"), saying what changed and why. Then a short body only if it adds something: the reason, anything surprising, and breaking changes. Match this repo's style if I paste recent commits. Don't describe line-by-line edits.

[PASTE git diff --staged]

items.name: Write Tests for This Code
items.summary: Writes unit tests that cover normal cases, edge cases and errors, in your test framework.
items.prompt:
Write tests for the code below using [FRAMEWORK, e.g. pytest, Jest, node:test]. First list the behaviors worth testing: normal cases, edge cases (empty, zero, very large, unicode), and error cases. Then write the tests, one behavior each, with names that describe the behavior. Don't test private details. If something is hard to test, tell me how to change the code to make it easier.

[PASTE CODE]

items.name: Explain This Error
items.summary: Explains an error message or stack trace in plain English and suggests the most likely fix.
useCases: why am i getting this error
items.prompt:
I got this error:
[PASTE ERROR / STACK TRACE]

What I was doing: [COMMAND OR ACTION]. Language and versions: [DETAILS]. Relevant code: [PASTE IF YOU HAVE IT]. Explain in plain English what the error means, the most likely cause, and the fix. If there are several possible causes, rank them and tell me how to check each one.

items.name: Regex Builder
items.summary: Writes and explains a regular expression from examples of what should and shouldn't match.
items.prompt: Write a regular expression for [LANGUAGE / TOOL] that matches [DESCRIPTION]. Should match: [EXAMPLES]. Should NOT match: [EXAMPLES]. Give the regex, a piece-by-piece explanation, and a table showing each of my examples and whether it matches. Mention any edge case it gets wrong.

items.name: Document This Code
items.summary: Writes docstrings, a README section or usage examples for code you paste.
items.prompt:
Document the code below. Write [docstrings / a README section / usage examples] in the style of [LANGUAGE CONVENTION, e.g. JSDoc, Google-style Python]. Cover what it does, inputs and outputs, errors it can raise, and one realistic example. Only document behavior you can see in the code, and tell me anything that looks like a bug while you're at it.

[PASTE CODE]
